metadata.description: Polynovea CMS: one VM, PostgreSQL Flexible Server 16 or on-server PostgreSQL, Blob backups, Key Vault, budget alert. About US$56/month managed or US$39/month on-this-server (East US list prices, November 2026).

Where the database runs. managed = Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server, found by the setup wizard by itself ("Created for you"). on-this-server = PostgreSQL on the VM's data disk, backed up to the Blob container.
Email for the budget alert: Azure writes when spending passes 80% of the budget, or is forecast to pass 100%.
Monthly budget for this resource group, in the subscription's billing currency.
Your SSH public key (one line starting with ssh-ed25519 or ssh-rsa). Azure requires one for a Linux VM; it is a public key, not a secret.

Your domain for the site, for example cms.example.com. With a domain the VM gets a free HTTPS certificate (Let's Encrypt) once the domain's A record points at the publicIp output, and setup is at https://<domain>/setup. Without one, ports 80 and 443 stay closed and setup goes through the SSH tunnel, which needs adminCidr.
Optional. Let's Encrypt may email this address about the certificate.
Leave blank for no SSH access at all. Set it to your own address (ending /32) to allow SSH from that address only. Needed for the SSH-tunnel route into the setup wizard when there is no domain.
VM size. Standard_B2s (2 vCPU, 4 GB) suits both modes.
Processor type. Must match vmSize: x64 for B2s and other Intel/AMD sizes, arm64 for Arm sizes such as Standard_B2pls_v2.
Size of the separate data disk mounted at /var/lib/polynovea (settings, uploads, and the database when it runs on the VM).
Database size (managed only). Burstable sizes are the cheapest.
Database storage in GB (managed only). It grows automatically.
Polynovea CMS image pinned by digest (name@sha256:...). Required on plain Ubuntu; on a Polynovea server image, blank uses the image it carries.
HTTPS proxy (Caddy) image pinned by digest. Required on plain Ubuntu; on a Polynovea server image, blank uses the image it carries.

Optional Polynovea server image: the published community gallery image (/CommunityGalleries/<public name>/Images/<definition>/Versions/<version>), or the resource ID of a managed image or gallery image version in your subscription. When blank, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS is used.
Location for all resources.
First day of the budget period. Leave as it is.
Leave as it is: a new random password is generated for every deployment and written straight into Key Vault.

#!/bin/sh
# GENERATED by deploy/scripts/sync-vm-bootstrap.mjs from the release package's VM files. Do not edit:
# change those files and run the script again. Files sha256: c6d0a99935a1516427de0d8aa9cebde613e5f69a72239335305c792430142974
#
# First boot of a Polynovea server made by a cloud template. The template has already written
# /etc/polynovea/polynovea.env (non-secret values only) and passes the cloud (aws or azure) as $1.
# - On a Polynovea server image everything is installed: start it again so it reads the new settings.
# - On plain Ubuntu 24.04, install exactly what the server image installs (provision.sh), then start it.
#
# Fails closed: images are used only by digest, and the release package checks the CMS image's
# signature (verify-images.sh) right after pulling and again before every start, so a unit whose
# check fails never starts. The log is in journalctl -u polynovea-bootstrap.
set -eu
CLOUD="${1:?usage: vm-bootstrap.sh aws|azure}"
ENV_FILE=/etc/polynovea/polynovea.env

value() { sed -n "s/^$1=//p" "$ENV_FILE" | tail -1 | tr -d '"'"'"'[:space:]'; }
for key in POLYNOVEA_IMAGE_REF POLYNOVEA_CADDY_IMAGE_REF; do
  ref="$(value "$key")"
  case "$ref" in
    "" | *@sha256:*) ;;
    *) echo "polynovea-bootstrap: $key must be pinned by digest (name@sha256:...)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

if [ ! -f /etc/systemd/system/polynovea.service ]; then
  FILES=/tmp/polynovea-files
  rm -rf "$FILES"
  install -d -m 0700 "$FILES"
cat > "$FILES/20auto-upgrades" <<'POLYNOVEA_FILE_END'

#!/bin/sh
# Starts the Polynovea CMS container (polynovea.service). The single source of the `docker run` line;
# docs/self-hosting/vm-images.md quotes it.
#
# Host networking: the CMS listens on 127.0.0.1:3000 of the VM itself, so the setup wizard's SSH-tunnel
# route works, and Caddy (polynovea-caddy.service, when POLYNOVEA_DOMAIN is set) reaches it from
# 127.0.0.1 as a trusted proxy.
set -eu

ENV_FILE=/etc/polynovea/polynovea.env
IMAGE_FILE=/etc/polynovea/image.env

value() { # key file
  [ -f "$2" ] || return 0
  sed -n "s/^$1=//p" "$2" | tail -1 | tr -d '"'"'"'[:space:]'
}

image="$(value POLYNOVEA_IMAGE_REF "$ENV_FILE")"
[ -n "$image" ] || image="$(value POLYNOVEA_IMAGE_REF "$IMAGE_FILE")"
case "$image" in
  *@sha256:*) ;;
  *) echo "run-cms: POLYNOVEA_IMAGE_REF must be pinned by digest (name@sha256:...)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

domain="$(value POLYNOVEA_DOMAIN "$ENV_FILE")"
if [ -n "$domain" ] && ! printf '%s' "$domain" | grep -Eq '^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?)+$'; then
  echo "run-cms: POLYNOVEA_DOMAIN is not a valid domain name" >&2
  exit 1
fi

docker image inspect "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1 || docker pull "$image"
docker rm -f polynovea >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

set --
[ -f "$ENV_FILE" ] && set -- "$@" --env-file "$ENV_FILE"
# These win over anything in the env file: the CMS must listen on loopback only.
set -- "$@" -e HOSTNAME=127.0.0.1 -e PORT=3000
if [ -n "$domain" ]; then
  set -- "$@" -e "POLYNOVEA_PUBLIC_URL=https://$domain" -e POLYNOVEA_TRUSTED_PROXIES=127.0.0.1
fi

exec docker run --rm --name polynovea \
  --network host \
  --security-opt no-new-privileges:true \
  --cap-drop ALL \
  --stop-timeout 90 \
  --log-driver journald --log-opt tag=polynovea \
  -v /var/lib/polynovea:/var/lib/polynovea \
  "$@" \
  "$image"
POLYNOVEA_FILE_END

#!/bin/sh
# Starts Caddy (polynovea-caddy.service) when POLYNOVEA_DOMAIN is set: HTTPS on 443 with a Let's Encrypt
# certificate (HTTP-01 on port 80), forwarding to the CMS on 127.0.0.1:3000.
set -eu

ENV_FILE=/etc/polynovea/polynovea.env
IMAGE_FILE=/etc/polynovea/image.env

value() { # key file
  [ -f "$2" ] || return 0
  sed -n "s/^$1=//p" "$2" | tail -1 | tr -d '"'"'"'[:space:]'
}

domain="$(value POLYNOVEA_DOMAIN "$ENV_FILE")"
printf '%s' "$domain" | grep -Eq '^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?)+$' || {
  echo "run-caddy: POLYNOVEA_DOMAIN is missing or not a valid domain name" >&2
  exit 1
}
# Optional: where Let's Encrypt sends certificate-expiry warnings. Without it, certificates are still issued.
email="$(value POLYNOVEA_ACME_EMAIL "$ENV_FILE")"
email_option=""
if [ -n "$email" ]; then
  printf '%s' "$email" | grep -Eq '^[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$' || {
    echo "run-caddy: POLYNOVEA_ACME_EMAIL is not a valid email address" >&2
    exit 1
  }
  email_option="email $email"
fi
image="$(value POLYNOVEA_CADDY_IMAGE_REF "$ENV_FILE")"
[ -n "$image" ] || image="$(value POLYNOVEA_CADDY_IMAGE_REF "$IMAGE_FILE")"
case "$image" in
  *@sha256:*) ;;
  *) echo "run-caddy: the Caddy image must be pinned by digest" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

docker image inspect "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1 || docker pull "$image"
docker rm -f polynovea-caddy >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

exec docker run --rm --name polynovea-caddy \
  --network host \
  --security-opt no-new-privileges:true \
  --cap-drop ALL --cap-add NET_BIND_SERVICE \
  --log-driver journald --log-opt tag=polynovea-caddy \
  -e "POLYNOVEA_DOMAIN=$domain" \
  -e "POLYNOVEA_ACME_EMAIL=$email" \
  -e "POLYNOVEA_CADDY_EMAIL_OPTION=$email_option" \
  -v /etc/polynovea/Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro \
  -v /var/lib/polynovea-caddy:/data \
  "$image"
POLYNOVEA_FILE_END

cat > "$FILES/data-disk.sh" <<'POLYNOVEA_FILE_END'
#!/bin/sh
# Finds the VM's data disk and gives it the POLYNOVEA_DATA label, so var-lib-polynovea.mount can mount
# it at /var/lib/polynovea. Runs at every boot (polynovea-data-disk.service) and does nothing once a
# disk with that label exists.
#
# It formats a disk ONLY when all of these hold: it is a whole disk, not the root disk, has no
# partitions, no filesystem or other signature, is not mounted, and it is the only such candidate.
# Candidates: POLYNOVEA_DATA_DEVICE from /etc/polynovea/polynovea.env when set; else Azure's data disk
# at LUN 0; else AWS EBS volumes (never instance-store disks). A disk that already has data is never
# touched: then set POLYNOVEA_DATA_DEVICE, or label it yourself (e2label <device> POLYNOVEA_DATA).
set -eu

LABEL=POLYNOVEA_DATA
ENV_FILE=/etc/polynovea/polynovea.env
WAIT_SECONDS=300

log() { echo "polynovea-data-disk: $*"; }

if [ -e "/dev/disk/by-label/$LABEL" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

configured=""
if [ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
  configured="$(sed -n 's/^POLYNOVEA_DATA_DEVICE=//p' "$ENV_FILE" | tail -1 | tr -d '"'"'"'[:space:]')"
fi
case "$configured" in
  "" | /dev/*) ;;
  *) log "POLYNOVEA_DATA_DEVICE must be a /dev path"; exit 1 ;;
esac

root_disk="$(lsblk -no PKNAME "$(findmnt -no SOURCE /)" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"

candidates() {
  if [ -n "$configured" ]; then
    readlink -f "$configured"
    return
  fi
  for azure in /dev/disk/azure/data/by-lun/0 /dev/disk/azure/scsi1/lun0; do
    if [ -e "$azure" ]; then
      readlink -f "$azure"
      return
    fi
  done
  lsblk -dpno NAME,TYPE,MODEL | awk '$2 == "disk" && /Amazon Elastic Block Store/ { print $1 }'
}

usable() { # device
  dev="$1"
  [ -b "$dev" ] || return 1
  [ "$(basename "$dev")" != "$root_disk" ] || return 1
  [ "$(lsblk -no TYPE "$dev" | head -1)" = disk ] || return 1
  [ "$(lsblk -no NAME "$dev" | wc -l)" -eq 1 ] || return 1          # no partitions
  [ -z "$(lsblk -no MOUNTPOINTS "$dev" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ] || return 1
  [ -z "$(wipefs --no-act --noheadings "$dev" 2>/dev/null)" ] || return 1   # no signature of any kind
  return 0
}

waited=0
while :; do
  found=""
  count=0
  for dev in $(candidates); do
    if usable "$dev"; then
      found="$dev"
      count=$((count + 1))
    fi
  done
  [ -e "/dev/disk/by-label/$LABEL" ] && exit 0
  if [ "$count" -eq 1 ]; then
    break
  fi
  if [ "$count" -gt 1 ]; then
    log "more than one empty disk; set POLYNOVEA_DATA_DEVICE in $ENV_FILE"
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ "$waited" -ge "$WAIT_SECONDS" ]; then
    log "no empty data disk found. Attach a separate disk for /var/lib/polynovea (the CMS will not use the root disk)."
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 5
  waited=$((waited + 5))
done

log "formatting $found as ext4 ($LABEL)"
mkfs.ext4 -q -L "$LABEL" -m 1 "$found"
udevadm settle
POLYNOVEA_FILE_END
cat > "$FILES/console-code.sh" <<'POLYNOVEA_FILE_END'
#!/bin/sh
# Copies the one-time setup code to the VM's serial console, so an owner can read it from the cloud
# console (AWS "Get system log", Azure serial console) without SSH. polynovea-console-code.service
# feeds it the CMS's log lines:
#
#   journalctl --follow --lines=0 --output=cat _SYSTEMD_UNIT=docker.service CONTAINER_NAME=polynovea | console-code.sh
#
# Limits (owner's decision, Phase 5):
# - only the setup-code line, nothing else from the log, and no other secret;
# - only while /api/health says the CMS is in setup mode. Once setup is finished it writes nothing,
#   and if the CMS cannot be asked, it writes nothing (fail closed);
# - the code is single-use and expires after an hour, but anyone in the cloud account who can read
#   console output can see it until setup is finished (docs/self-hosting/setup/setup-code.md).
#
# Environment (tests): POLYNOVEA_CONSOLE (default /dev/console), POLYNOVEA_HEALTH_URL
# (default http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health), POLYNOVEA_HEALTH_WAIT (seconds, default 90).
set -u

CONSOLE="${POLYNOVEA_CONSOLE:-/dev/console}"
HEALTH_URL="${POLYNOVEA_HEALTH_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health}"
WAIT="${POLYNOVEA_HEALTH_WAIT:-90}"

# The code is printed while the server starts, before it answers; wait for its answer.
in_setup_mode() {
  waited=0
  while [ "$waited" -le "$WAIT" ]; do
    state="$(curl -fsS --max-time 3 "$HEALTH_URL" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*"state" *: *"\([a-z]*\)".*/\1/p')"
    case "$state" in
      setup) return 0 ;;
      running | unavailable) return 1 ;;
    esac
    sleep 2
    waited=$((waited + 2))
  done
  return 1
}

while IFS= read -r line; do
  # Exactly the CMS's setup-code line; the code itself is Crockford base32 in groups.
  code="$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | sed -n 's/^\[setup\] Setup code: \([A-Za-z0-9-]\{16,80\}\)  *(works once.*$/\1/p')"
  [ -n "$code" ] || continue
  if in_setup_mode; then
    printf 'Polynovea CMS setup code: %s (works once, for 1 hour; a restart issues a new one)\n' "$code" >"$CONSOLE"
  fi
done
POLYNOVEA_FILE_END
cat > "$FILES/verify-images.sh" <<'POLYNOVEA_FILE_END'
#!/bin/sh
# Checks the images before every start (ExecStartPre of polynovea.service and polynovea-caddy.service),
# on a VM made from our image and on the templates' plain-Ubuntu bootstrap alike. Any failure exits
# non-zero, so systemd does not start the unit (fail closed).
#
#   verify-images.sh        the CMS image: pinned by digest AND signed with the Polynovea release key
#   verify-images.sh caddy  the Caddy image: pinned by digest (it is Caddy's own image, not signed by us)
#
# Trust material is local and fixed: the release public key installed by provision.sh at
# /etc/polynovea/release.pub, and cosign's own image pinned by digest. The signature itself is read
# from the image's own (pinned) registry; nothing else is fetched. A digest that verified once with
# this exact key is remembered (/var/lib/polynovea-verified), so a restart while the registry is
# unreachable still starts the image it already checked, and never a different one.
#
# Environment (tests only): POLYNOVEA_ETC (default /etc/polynovea), POLYNOVEA_VERIFIED_DIR
# (default /var/lib/polynovea-verified).
set -eu

ETC="${POLYNOVEA_ETC:-/etc/polynovea}"
ENV_FILE="$ETC/polynovea.env"
IMAGE_FILE="$ETC/image.env"
PUBKEY="$ETC/release.pub"
VERIFIED_DIR="${POLYNOVEA_VERIFIED_DIR:-/var/lib/polynovea-verified}"
COSIGN_IMAGE="ghcr.io/sigstore/cosign/cosign:v2.6.1@sha256:68839b7f13dac5a6744a5d8818e984dd39183374e37855c19e14d623d9bc9037"
PINNED='^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9./:_-]*@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$'

fail() { echo "verify-images: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

value() { # key file
  [ -f "$2" ] || return 0
  sed -n "s/^$1=//p" "$2" | tail -1 | tr -d '"'"'"'[:space:]'
}

image_ref() { # key
  ref="$(value "$1" "$ENV_FILE")"
  [ -n "$ref" ] || ref="$(value "$1" "$IMAGE_FILE")"
  printf '%s' "$ref" | grep -Eq "$PINNED" || fail "$1 is missing or not pinned by digest (name@sha256:<64 hex>)"
  printf '%s' "$ref"
}

# Present locally under exactly this digest (a pull by digest checks the content against it).
ensure_local() { # ref
  docker image inspect "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || docker pull -q "$1" >/dev/null || fail "could not pull $1"
}

case "${1:-cms}" in
  caddy)
    ref="$(image_ref POLYNOVEA_CADDY_IMAGE_REF)"
    ensure_local "$ref"
    echo "verify-images: Caddy image pinned: $ref"
    exit 0
    ;;
  cms) ;;
  *) fail "usage: verify-images.sh [cms|caddy]" ;;
esac

ref="$(image_ref POLYNOVEA_IMAGE_REF)"
if ! grep -q "BEGIN PUBLIC KEY" "$PUBKEY" 2>/dev/null; then fail "no release public key at $PUBKEY; refusing to start an unverified image"; fi
key_sum="$(sha256sum "$PUBKEY" | cut -c1-64)"
digest="${ref##*@sha256:}"
marker="$VERIFIED_DIR/$digest.$key_sum"

ensure_local "$ref"
if [ -f "$marker" ]; then
  echo "verify-images: $ref already verified with this release key"
  exit 0
fi

docker image inspect "$COSIGN_IMAGE" >/dev/null 2>&1 || docker pull -q "$COSIGN_IMAGE" >/dev/null || fail "could not pull the pinned cosign image"
errors="$(mktemp)"
if ! docker run --rm --network host -v "$PUBKEY:/release.pub:ro" "$COSIGN_IMAGE" \
  verify --key /release.pub --insecure-ignore-tlog=true "$ref" >/dev/null 2>"$errors"; then
  tail -5 "$errors" >&2 || true
  rm -f "$errors"
  fail "the signature of $ref does not verify with the Polynovea release key; not starting it"
fi
rm -f "$errors"

umask 077
mkdir -p "$VERIFIED_DIR"
: >"$marker"
echo "verify-images: $ref signature verified"
POLYNOVEA_FILE_END
cat > "$FILES/Caddyfile" <<'POLYNOVEA_FILE_END'
# HTTPS in front of Polynovea CMS (docker/compose.yaml "proxy" profile, and the VM's
# polynovea-caddy.service). Caddy gets and renews a Let's Encrypt certificate for POLYNOVEA_DOMAIN
# (it needs ports 80 and 443) and forwards to the CMS on 127.0.0.1:3000, adding X-Forwarded-For,
# X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-Host, which the CMS believes only because POLYNOVEA_TRUSTED_PROXIES
# is 127.0.0.1.
#
# POLYNOVEA_CADDY_EMAIL_OPTION is either empty or "email <address>", built from the optional
# POLYNOVEA_ACME_EMAIL by run-caddy.sh (VM) or docker/caddy-start.sh (compose), both of which validate
# it and POLYNOVEA_DOMAIN first. Caddy substitutes these before parsing, so an empty option leaves
# no email at all: Let's Encrypt issues certificates without one; with one, it sends expiry warnings.
{
	admin off
	{$POLYNOVEA_CADDY_EMAIL_OPTION}
}

{$POLYNOVEA_DOMAIN} {
	encode zstd gzip
	reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
}
POLYNOVEA_FILE_END

cat > "$FILES/polynovea-console-code.service" <<'POLYNOVEA_FILE_END'
[Unit]
Description=Polynovea CMS: show the one-time setup code on the serial console while in setup mode
After=systemd-journald.service docker.service
Before=polynovea.service

[Service]
Type=simple

cat > "$FILES/polynovea-caddy.service" <<'POLYNOVEA_FILE_END'

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
POLYNOVEA_FILE_END
cat > "$FILES/provision.sh" <<'POLYNOVEA_FILE_END'
#!/bin/sh
# Turns an Ubuntu 24.04 LTS VM into a Polynovea CMS server. Two callers, one script, same end state:
#
# - Packer, while building the AMI or Azure image (aws.pkr.hcl, azure.pkr.hcl). The services are
#   enabled and start when a VM is launched from the image.
# - The cloud templates' bootstrap on a plain Ubuntu VM, with POLYNOVEA_START_NOW=1: the same steps,
#   then the services start at once. Start it with systemd-run from user data, not inline: the first
#   step waits for cloud-init to finish, which would deadlock inside cloud-init itself.
#
# Safe to run again on a box that is already set up (it changes nothing that is already right, and
# never touches /etc/polynovea/polynovea.env or the data disk's contents).
#
# Needs: POLYNOVEA_IMAGE_REF (pinned by digest), POLYNOVEA_CADDY_IMAGE_REF, POLYNOVEA_RELEASE_ID,
# POLYNOVEA_CLOUD (aws|azure), and the files from release/packer/files plus docker/Caddyfile in
# /tmp/polynovea-files (or POLYNOVEA_FILES). They must include polynovea-release.pub, the release
# signing key's public half: without it this script stops, because no image could be verified.
set -eu

: "${POLYNOVEA_IMAGE_REF:?}" "${POLYNOVEA_CADDY_IMAGE_REF:?}" "${POLYNOVEA_RELEASE_ID:?}" "${POLYNOVEA_CLOUD:?}"
case "$POLYNOVEA_IMAGE_REF" in *@sha256:*) ;; *) echo "POLYNOVEA_IMAGE_REF must be pinned by digest" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
case "$POLYNOVEA_CADDY_IMAGE_REF" in *@sha256:*) ;; *) echo "POLYNOVEA_CADDY_IMAGE_REF must be pinned by digest" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
FILES="${POLYNOVEA_FILES:-/tmp/polynovea-files}"
COSIGN_IMAGE="ghcr.io/sigstore/cosign/cosign:v2.6.1@sha256:68839b7f13dac5a6744a5d8818e984dd39183374e37855c19e14d623d9bc9037"
grep -q "BEGIN PUBLIC KEY" "$FILES/polynovea-release.pub" 2>/dev/null || {
  echo "provision: $FILES/polynovea-release.pub (the release public key) is missing" >&2
  exit 1
}
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Let cloud-init finish its own apt work first.
cloud-init status --wait >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# 1. Patched base, Docker from Ubuntu's archive (so it gets Ubuntu's security updates), and automatic
#    security updates.
apt-get update
apt-get -y -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold dist-upgrade
apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends docker.io unattended-upgrades ca-certificates curl e2fsprogs util-linux
install -m 0644 "$FILES/20auto-upgrades" /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/20auto-upgrades
install -m 0644 "$FILES/52polynovea-unattended-upgrades" /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/52polynovea-unattended-upgrades

# 2. Docker: logs to the journal (kept 14 days). live-restore stays off on purpose: the CMS runs in the
#    foreground of polynovea.service (docker run --rm), so when dockerd restarts (for example a security
#    update), systemd restarts the service and verify-images.sh checks the image again before it starts.
install -d -m 0755 /etc/docker /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d
install -m 0644 "$FILES/daemon.json" /etc/docker/daemon.json
install -m 0644 "$FILES/journald-polynovea.conf" /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/polynovea.conf

# 3. Polynovea: scripts, units, the HTTPS proxy's config, and which image this VM image carries.
install -d -m 0755 /opt/polynovea /etc/polynovea
install -m 0755 "$FILES/run-cms.sh" "$FILES/run-caddy.sh" "$FILES/has-domain.sh" "$FILES/data-disk.sh" "$FILES/console-code.sh" "$FILES/verify-images.sh" /opt/polynovea/
install -m 0644 "$FILES/Caddyfile" /etc/polynovea/Caddyfile
install -m 0644 "$FILES/polynovea-release.pub" /etc/polynovea/release.pub
sed -i 's/\r$//' /opt/polynovea/*.sh /etc/polynovea/Caddyfile /etc/polynovea/release.pub /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/52polynovea-unattended-upgrades /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/20auto-upgrades
cat >/etc/polynovea/image.env <<EOF
# Written by provision.sh. /etc/polynovea/polynovea.env may override POLYNOVEA_IMAGE_REF.
POLYNOVEA_IMAGE_REF=$POLYNOVEA_IMAGE_REF
POLYNOVEA_CADDY_IMAGE_REF=$POLYNOVEA_CADDY_IMAGE_REF
POLYNOVEA_RELEASE_ID=$POLYNOVEA_RELEASE_ID
POLYNOVEA_CLOUD=$POLYNOVEA_CLOUD
EOF
chmod 0644 /etc/polynovea/image.env
UNITS="polynovea-data-disk.service var-lib-polynovea.mount polynovea-console-code.service polynovea.service polynovea-caddy.service"
for unit in $UNITS; do
  install -m 0644 "$FILES/$unit" "/etc/systemd/system/$unit"
  sed -i 's/\r$//' "/etc/systemd/system/$unit"
done
# Mount point and Caddy's state. Left alone when they exist (the data disk may already be mounted).
[ -d /var/lib/polynovea ] || install -d -m 0755 /var/lib/polynovea
[ -d /var/lib/polynovea-caddy ] || install -d -m 0700 /var/lib/polynovea-caddy
[ -d /var/lib/polynovea-verified ] || install -d -m 0700 /var/lib/polynovea-verified

# 4. The images, pulled by digest (content-addressed), and the CMS image's release signature checked
#    now, so a build or bootstrap with a bad image stops here. The units check again before every start.
systemctl enable --now docker.service
docker pull "$POLYNOVEA_IMAGE_REF"
docker pull "$POLYNOVEA_CADDY_IMAGE_REF"
docker pull "$COSIGN_IMAGE"
/opt/polynovea/verify-images.sh
/opt/polynovea/verify-images.sh caddy

systemctl daemon-reload
# shellcheck disable=SC2086 # UNITS is a list
systemctl enable docker.service $UNITS

# 5. Clean up.
apt-get -y autoremove --purge
apt-get clean
rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* "$FILES"

# 6. Plain-Ubuntu bootstrap only: start now (a VM made from the image starts them at boot).
if [ "${POLYNOVEA_START_NOW:-0}" = 1 ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # UNITS is a list
  systemctl start --no-block $UNITS
fi
POLYNOVEA_FILE_END
# No polynovea-release.pub in this build of the release package: provision.sh refuses to run without
# it, so nothing starts (fail closed) until a release ships its public key.

  # provision.sh installs, pulls by digest, verifies and, with POLYNOVEA_START_NOW=1, starts the units.
  POLYNOVEA_IMAGE_REF="$(value POLYNOVEA_IMAGE_REF)" \
  POLYNOVEA_CADDY_IMAGE_REF="$(value POLYNOVEA_CADDY_IMAGE_REF)" \
  POLYNOVEA_RELEASE_ID=cloud-template \
  POLYNOVEA_CLOUD="$CLOUD" \
  POLYNOVEA_FILES="$FILES" \
  POLYNOVEA_START_NOW=1 \
    sh "$FILES/provision.sh"
else
  # A Polynovea server image started its units at boot, before user data wrote the settings: restart
  # them so they read the settings (each start re-runs the image check).
  systemctl daemon-reload
  systemctl start polynovea-data-disk.service var-lib-polynovea.mount
  systemctl restart polynovea-console-code.service polynovea.service polynovea-caddy.service
fi

metadata.description: Where to open the setup wizard. With a domain, first point its A record at publicIp. The setup code is in the VM's log (see the README).
